title: Marrying Sue Baker and her epilepsy
summary: He says he married Sue Baker in 1927, she died in 1946, and tells how he found her ill and took her to hospital.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: I'd hang around with all the beautiful girls. I used to go in the place and have all the chorus girls with me. And I'd call my wife up, I'd say, come on up here, so and so. I went to Chicago and met some more chorus girls, and I said, get them on the first place and come on over.
Who was your wife then, Tom?
Yeah, my wife Mona and I knew her.
She was an epileptic, and I didn't know it.

And one day I came home-- I was with the band, you know. And I came home and I was going to Boston, I think. And she was fall out on the floor. I said, huh? You can't stay sober one day. And the next -- I woke up in the morning and she was on the sofa. And she couldn't talk. And I called the doctor up and -- called Doc Grogan and I says, she can't talk and I got to get out of her.
So I think I took her to the hospital. I took her up to the Seidenham. And when I come back, I took her out of the Seidenham, I bodily took her out of the Seidenham and took her over to the Bellevue.
Hold it just a minute, Tom.
